moved.sentence: Run platform builds in CI for every target the project ships; a green Android build does not prove the iOS framework links.

judged.note: should-build-every-target-in-ci keeps running CI builds for every shipped target (unkeyed, now SHOULD); the rationale keeps that a green Android build does not prove the iOS framework links.

moved.sentence: Every `expect` declaration **MUST** have a matching `actual` in the same package for every target; the compiler enforces this.

judged.note: must-match-every-expect-with-actual keeps the MUST, same-package and every-target scope; the rationale keeps that the compiler enforces it.

moved.sentence: Prefer interfaces plus dependency injection over `expect`/`actual` when the seam is non-trivial — it is easier to test and delete.

judged.note: should-prefer-interfaces-over-expect-actual keeps the preference and its non-trivial-seam condition; the rationale keeps the easier-to-test-and-delete reason.

moved.sentence: Use the hierarchical source-set structure (e.g., an intermediate `appleMain` shared by `iosMain`/`macosMain`) so common-but-not-universal code is not duplicated.

judged.note: should-use-hierarchical-source-sets keeps the hierarchical source-set instruction, the appleMain example and the no-duplication reason.

moved.sentence: Android consumes the shared module directly as a Gradle dependency. iOS consumes it as an Apple framework (XCFramework / CocoaPods / SPM) — design the public API to be Swift-friendly: avoid Kotlin-only constructs (sealed-class exhaustiveness, default args) at the boundary.

judged.note: should-design-swift-friendly-api keeps the Swift-friendly API instruction and the Kotlin-only constructs to avoid; the rationale keeps how Android (Gradle) and iOS (XCFramework/CocoaPods/SPM) consume the module.

moved.sentence: Expose `suspend` functions and `Flow` through a documented bridge (e.g., a `Skie`-style or hand-written wrapper) so Swift callers get idiomatic async; do not leak raw coroutines across the boundary.

judged.note: should-bridge-suspend-and-flow keeps the documented bridge, Skie/hand-written examples and idiomatic-async reason; should-not-leak-raw-coroutines keeps the prohibition.

moved.sentence: Keep platform-idiomatic UI (SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, web framework) on the consuming side unless a shared-UI decision is made deliberately.

judged.note: should-keep-platform-ui-on-consumer keeps platform-idiomatic UI on the consumer side and the deliberate-shared-UI exception.

moved.sentence: A shared ViewModel/presentation layer **MAY** be shared when the team accepts coupling presentation state to KMP; treat it as a deliberate scope expansion, not a default.

judged.note: may-share-presentation-layer keeps the MAY and its accepts-coupling condition; should-treat-shared-presentation-as-deliberate keeps deliberate-scope-expansion-not-default.

moved.sentence: Apply boundaries per [adc.principle.manage-complexity-through-boundaries](cookbook:555ad5e1-800f-4848-8c58-6f726bdcb42b): expose narrow interfaces from the shared module so platforms stay swappable.

judged.note: should-expose-narrow-interfaces keeps the boundaries-principle link and narrow interfaces so platforms stay swappable.

moved.sentence: Pin the CMP version explicitly in the build and re-check the release notes before relying on a specific UI feature.

judged.note: should-pin-cmp-version keeps pinning the CMP version explicitly in the build; should-recheck-cmp-release-notes keeps re-checking notes before relying on a UI feature.

moved.sentence: iOS UI parity (text selection, native scrolling, accessibility/VoiceOver, gestures) is improving release-over-release but **still evolving** — FORECAST any unreleased item against the version you pin, and validate accessibility on-device.

judged.note: The rationale keeps the still-evolving iOS parity list; the two rules keep forecasting unreleased items against the pinned version and on-device accessibility validation, scoped as the old shared-CMP-UI section was.

moved.sentence: Choose shared CMP UI **only** when the team accepts current iOS maturity and values UI reuse over fully native look-and-feel; otherwise keep SwiftUI on iOS and Compose on Android while still sharing all non-UI logic.

judged.note: should-choose-shared-ui-only-when-accepted keeps the 'only when' conditions (accepts iOS maturity, values reuse over native feel) and its 'otherwise keep SwiftUI/Compose, still share non-UI logic' sub-item.

moved.sentence: Present this as a deliberate decision per app, not a mandate.

judged.note: should-present-shared-ui-as-per-app-decision keeps presenting shared CMP UI as a deliberate per-app decision, not a mandate.
